questions.q: What makes Project 2's natural-language-to-SQL skill fundamentally different from Project 1's RAG retrieval?
options: Project 2 doesn't use an LLM at all
RAG retrieves existing text, while Project 2 must generate a new, correct query against a schema it wasn't trained on and then execute it
Project 2 only works with unstructured documents
There is no real difference between the two skills
questions.explain: RAG surfaces text that already roughly answers the question. An AI data analyst has to generate a query from scratch and run it against live, structured data -- a different and riskier failure mode.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a database with at least two or three related tables rather than one flat table?
options: A single flat table is more secure
Multiple related tables give the natural-language-to-SQL work in Lesson 10 something interesting to do, like joins
Flat tables cannot be queried with SQL
It has no effect on the project
questions.explain: A flat, single-table database has no joins or relationships to reason about, so it doesn't exercise the query-generation skill this project is meant to build.

questions.q: What is the purpose of writing down three to five real questions before building anything?
options: They become your test cases for Lesson 10 and your demo script for Lesson 12
They are submitted to Anthropic for approval
They replace the need for a database connection
They are only used in Lesson 9
questions.explain: Concrete questions give you something to validate the NL-to-SQL function against and something to walk through when presenting the finished project.

questions.q: Which lesson in this chapter specifically builds the read-only, parameterized database connection?
options: Lesson 8
Lesson 9
Lesson 11
Lesson 12
questions.explain: Lesson 9, 'Connecting to a Database Safely,' is the foundation every later lesson in this chapter builds on.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should the external API you choose for Project 2 add to your project?
options: Nothing -- the API is optional and can be skipped entirely
A second copy of the same data already in your database
Something the database itself doesn't have, like live exchange rates or weather
A replacement for the database connection
questions.explain: The point of Lesson 11 is combining a SQL result with a live external call that adds information the database doesn't already contain.
